recent.narrative: The Monument Creek and Munson Ridge SNOTEL reported a 24 hour snow depth change of 9 inches at 1300 on 12/12/25, exceeding the minimum 7 inches in 24 hours criteria.
Local observers and trained spotters reported 12 inches of snow over a 24 hour period at Chena River Recreation Area.

Heavy snow fell across the Upper Chena River Valley. The Monument Creek SNOTEL (MNCA) reported 7 inches of snow between noon on October 21st and 10 am on October 22nd, with a storm total amount of 15 inches. Mt. Ryan SNOTEL (MTRA2) reported 8 inches of snow between 7 pm on the 20th and 7 pm on the 21st, with a storm total of 18 inches. Munson Ridge SNOTEL (MSOA2) reported 12 inches of snow between midnight on the 21st and midnight on the 22nd, with a storm total amount of 18 inches. The Upper Chena SNOTEL (UCEA2)reported 9 inches of snow between the 21st and 22nd, with a storm total amounts of 13 inches.
Heavy snow fell across the Chatanika River Valley. The Little Chena Ridge SNOTEL (LCRA2) reported an increase in snow depth of 12 inches in 24 hours.

Nearly 5 inches of rain fell between August 15th through August 19th, as reported by the Dahl Creek precipitation gage. The Kobuk River at Kobuk responded by rising into town after the first crest on August 20th. Kobuk experienced water over roadways and beneath homes and some citizens were unable to vote due to the flooding. An additional 2 inches of rain fell between August 21st and 23rd, resulting in water once again rising into town.

Emergency management personnel with the Tanana Chiefs Conference and local officials from Allakaket reported a prolonged moderate to major flood that surrounded most of the lower community, Old Town, and the old runway. Several roads including the airport access road and Main Street washed out. The river officially crested at 64.54 feet on August 31st.

Heavy rainfall over the northern Interior caused rapid rises on the Alatna and Kuyokuk Rivers. The water came up 4 to 6 feet in three days on the Alatna River and the Koyukuk was very high with debris and flooding. In Allakaket, water flooding the boat launch, as well as fish camps along the river.

DOT/Alaska 511 reported blizzard conditions on their webpage, with the Dalton Highway closed near Sagwon at 1104 on 12/12/25. The reported estimated 8 inches of total snow with sites to the north, east, and south reporting 70 to 100 mph winds. Cloudy skies, falling snow, strong winds, and blizzard/whiteout conditions continued for many continuous hours and ended at 0614 on 12/13/25.

Early morning 511 reports (Alaska DOT) and blowing snow satellite products indicated blizzard conditions. 511 Report had peak wind of 52 mph, large snow drift near MM392 and visibility down to 1 delineator, approximately 500 feet.
Local DOT reported blizzard conditions near Ice Cut Hill along the Dalton Highway. Considerable blowing snow was reported along with northeast winds of 48 mph.
The Bonzana Creek SNOTEL reported a 24 hour snow depth change of 7.6 inches at 1200 on 12/12/25, exceeding the minimum 7 inches in 24 hours criteria.
Local spotter reports 11 inches of snow in 24 hours at Birch Lakes.

Z840.name: EIELSON AIR FORCE BASE AND SALCHA

recent.area: EIELSON AIR FORCE BASE AND SALCHA
recent.narrative: A trained spotter in Harding Lake reported a 24 hour total of 8 inches new snowfall from the morning of December 24th through the morning of December 25th. The eventual storm total at Harding Lake was 12 inches. Meanwhile public reports from social media indicated storm total snowfall of 12 to 14 inches at Salcha and 8 inches at Eielson Air Force Base.

recent.area: EIELSON AIR FORCE BASE AND SALCHA
recent.narrative: Our COOP observer, Tom Griffith, reported a 24 hour snowfall total from 0900 on 12/12/25 to 0900 12/13/25. Additionally, there was a social media report of 10 inches of snowfall on Old Valdez trail by Harding Lake between 1747 on 12/12/25 to 0900 on 12/13/25.

recent.area: EIELSON AIR FORCE BASE AND SALCHA
recent.narrative: Local facebook post indicated 8 of new snow at Salcha. Eielson AFB reported 9 of snow in a 24 hour period.
Local spotter from Nenana Hills reported 9 inches of snow in 24 hours.
Local trained spotter reports 12 new snow in 24 hours at Pleasant Valley.
The official snowfall observation from the NWS Fairbanks office reported a 24 hour snow total of 7.6.
Numerous spotter reports across the Fairbanks metro area reported 8 to 15 inches of new snow in 24 hours. This includes 15 at Ester, 13 at North Pole, and 12 2 miles southwest of College.
The Umiat Air Field RAWS (UMTA2) reported an air temperature of -48F and wind speeds of up to 7mph resulting in a wind chill value of -71F.

Kodiak Airport reported 4.27 inches of rain which drove area rivers up, and flooded low lying roads, ditches and areas with poor drainage.  The Terror River crested at 5.26 ft at 10:30PM AKST; this is 0.26 ft above minor flood stage.

The Fort Greely/Big Delta ASOS reported a period of strong southerly winds through Isabel pass the persisted for just over 24 hours with sustained winds of 45 to 50 mph and consistent gusts to around 70 mph. The strongest gust occurred just prior to midnight on the 28th with a reading of 75 mph. There were reports on social media indicating that several trees were downed in and around Delta Junction as well as some minor roof damage.

Strong gap winds emerged out of Isabel Pass and crossed into the Tanana Valley near Delta Junction where the Delta Junction ASOS (PABI) reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph. Nearby mesonet site MGTA2 registered a maximum wind gust of 76 mph. Trees were reported down at Delta Junction and south of Greely. In addition social media showed a green house with the roof ripped off near Delta Junction.

Winds gusted as high as 71 mph at Ft Greely (PABI) with other locations consistently experiencing wind gusts in excess of 50 mph for several hours. Numerous trees were downed as well as multiple power outages in and around Delta Junction. As many as 900 residents were without power as a result.
Strong southerly winds through Isabel Pass emerged into the Delta Junction area with a station MGTA2 at the Fort Greely main gate seeing about an hour of wind gusts near 60 mph.

recent.narrative: The low's front produced a strong barrier jet that brought gusty winds of over 70 mph in the Cordova airport and Cordova itself. A weather station located at the northern periphery of Cordova reported strong winds gusting to over 65 mph for a two hour period from 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM AKST on January 12th. The highest wind gust was 74 mph at 8:12 AM AKST.

The Cordova ASOS (PACV) reported wind gusts of over 70 mph at from 3:50 PM to 4:53 PM AKST on January 6th as the front moved onshore. A peak wind gust of 82 mph was reported by the station at 4:53 PM AKST. A weather station (CRVA2) within Cordova itself reported very strong wind gusts of over 80 mph with a peak wind gust of 88 mph around the same time period.

The Utqiagvik (Barrow) ASOS site (PABR) reported meeting blizzard criteria at 0550 on 12/12/25. Blizzard conditions were observed at the site between 0250 to 0845 on 12/12/25. A peak wind gust of 55 mph and visibility less than 1/4 miles was reported at 0640 on 12/12/25.

Winds picked up resulting in blowing snow and blizzard conditions during the early morning at Barrow ASOS (PABR). Blizzard conditions persisted for almost 18 hours before visibilities increased. The peak wind recorded during the event was 45 mph.

Blizzard conditions developed during the morning hours at Utqiagvik with the PABR AWOS reporting visibility down to .25 miles and winds gusting to 68 mph. The ASOS stopped reporting during the event, but public reports supported the blizzard continuing into the afternoon hours.

Selawik AWOS (PASK) reported a surface temperature of -36F and 18kt wind speed resulting in a wind chill of -70F.

Alaska DOT reported Blizzard conditions through Windy Pass along the Parks Highway. DOT crews reported not being able to tell when the snow stopped due to the amount of blowing snow and poor visibility.

The ice jam caused water to rapidly rise and flood the road connecting the Upper Kalskag and Lower Kalskag communities.  School children were taken back and forth by boat to travel between the two villages while flood waters were at their highest.  By May 7th, the downstream ice jam broke up and allowed water levels to recede to normal levels.

Weather observation sites in some villages such as Mekoryuk and Kipnuk stopped reporting data during the event after receiving wind gusts greater than 70 mph, so peak winds in those locations are unknown. The Kipnuk gage datum recorded water levels of 5.86 ft above the normal highest tide line before the instrument experienced an outage (the actual crest was likely higher). A tribal leader in Kipnuk noted coastal flooding of low lying areas and some boardwalks. A tribal leader in Tuntutuliak noted that a boat was underwater with water levels still being elevated at 1:00 PM AKDT October 8.

recent.area: KUSKOKWIM DELTA COAST AND NUNIVAK ISLAND
recent.narrative: The Toksook Bay and Chefornak webcams displayed visibility lower than half a mile at 7:30 PM AKDT on April 3rd. Conditions further deteriorated with winds becoming sustained at 30 to 40 mph by 11:00 PM AKDT the same day. Blizzard conditions persisted in these settlements until the evening hours of April 4th.

The False Pass ASOS (PAKF) reported heavy snow, winds gusting to over 40 mph, and visibilities less than a quarter of a mile starting at 7:36 AM AKDT on April 13th and continuing until 11:15 AM AKDT the same day. The Cold Bay ASOS (PACD) reported similar conditions from 9:20 AM AKDT April 13th until 11:55 AM AKDT the same day.

A weather station in Potter Marsh (PMHA2) reported gusty winds all throughout August 28th. Winds peaked in the late morning when winds gusts frequented over 70 mph. At 9:02 AM AKDT, a wind gust of 86 mph was reported by PMHA2. Winds remained gusty all day and a second peak of greater than 70 mph wind gusts occurred from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM AKDT before winds dropped off. Other weather stations on the Anchorage Hillside reported winds gusting to over 65 mph during the same time periods as the peak wind gusts in Potter Marsh.

A weather station in Bear Valley (G5830) reported gusty winds in excess of 70 mph beginning April 16th at 8:16 AM AKDT. Wind gusts peaked at 10:31 AM AKDT the same day, gusting to 91 mph until 10:36 AM AKDT. Gusty winds commonly surpassing 80 mph remained until 1:52 PM that day.

A weather station (FW8205) in Potter Valley winds gusting over 65 mph from 1:21 AM to 3:10 AM AKDT on April 14th. Wind gusts peaked at 83 mph from 1:36 to 1:41 AM AKDT the same day. Other weather stations in the Anchorage Hillside reported winds gusting to over 70 mph for the same time period. An NWS employee observed a 12 - 15 inch diameter conifer down in Potter Valley alongside Bluebell Dr after the event.

The Whittier Access Tunnel weather station (WRTA2) and the Portage ASOS (PATO) reported gusty winds of over 60 mph in the morning hours of April 16, and lasting through the evening. The Whittier Access Tunnel station had a peak wind gust of 82 mph at 7:20 PM AKDT the same day. Portage had two peak gusts of 73 mph at 5:27 AM and 11:37 AM AKDT also on the 16th.

Water over the Dalton Highway caused the road to wash out between mile markers 142 and 144 just north of Prospect Creek.  The Alaska DOT was forced to completely close the roadway between mile markers 112 and 156. All traffic was stopped at the Jim River DOT Camp.

The TKRA2 (Tok River Valley), WMEWC (Mentasta), CZOA2 (Chistochina), and AK906 (Tok Cutoff) weather stations reported temperatures at or above 75F, breezy winds, and relative humidity levels near 25% from 4 PM to 8 PM AKDT on August 6th.

Winds remained gusty until the evening hours. The Alaska State Fair announced closure of some rides on Aug 28 due to high winds, with some performances also being canceled or relocated. Matanuska Electric reported power outages in various locations including Palmer and Wasilla on August 28th.

The Anchorage Ted Stevens International Airport ASOS (PANC) reported a wind gust of 55 mph at 5:53 PM AKDT August 28th. Wind gusts around 50 mph remained until 8:00 PM AKDT the same day. The Fort Richardson ASOS (PAFR) reported a wind gust of 58 mph from 7:55 PM to 8:00 PM AKDT on the 28th, which were the highest winds speeds reported in the Anchorage Bowl. The Lake Hood ASOS (PALH) reported a wind gust of 47 mph at 8:47 PM AKDT. An NWS Employee reported a downed tree on Beechcraft road north of Lake Hood at 8:45 PM AKDT August 28th. Chugach Electric reported that 1760 customers were without power in Northeast Anchorage on the evening of August 28th. Matanuska Electric reported that 157 customers in Eagle River lost power the same day.

At the Eagle Airport (PAEG) winds increased and wind chill dropped well below -60F during the early morning hours of December 24th. With wind gusts as high as 60 mph, wind chill values were as low as -75F during the morning hours of Christmas Eve.

recent.narrative: Public reports and photos delivered to the NWS River Forecast Center in Alaska indicated that the road to Wiseman was completely covered, thus preventing any travel into or out of Wiseman by automobile. It was estimated that the Middle Fork of the Koyukuk rose high enough to cover the road with water 18 inches deep.

Gusty winds were reported by various weather stations around Kodiak City. The Matson Crane (elevation 340 ft) recorded a peak wind gust of 83 mph at 9:02 AM AKDT October 29. The Kodiak Airport reported gusty winds over 55 mph from 5:45 AM to 10:03 AM AKDT with a peak wind gust of 71 mph at 8:30 AM AKDT October 29.

The St. George ASOS (PAPB) started measuring wind gusts above 70 mph by 7:50 AKDT Oct 11. Winds continued to gust over 70 mph for several hours with the peak wind gust reaching 91 mph at 10:15 PM AKDT the same day. The Saint Paul ASOS (PASN) reported winds gusting over 65 mph from 8:05 PM AKDT to 1:25 AM AKDT October 12. The peak wind gust on Saint Paul was a 79 mph wind gust at 10:10 PM AKDT October 11. No structural impacts were reported with these winds.

The community of Tuntutuliak experienced major flooding due to the surge flowing up into the Kuskokwim River channel, with the worst flooding observed near the time of normal high tide on the morning of October 12th.  Based on early high water survey data conducted by the Department of Geological and Geophysical Survey, water levels reached several feet above the normal high tide height in Tuntutuliak, similar to what was observed father upstream along the Kuskokwim River. The Alaska State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC) reported that multiple homes were moved from their foundations by water and that an unknown volume of waste oil was spilled from a service station in the community as a result of the water inundation.

The Imnaviat Creek SNOTEL reported 7 inches of snow between 0500 on 12/12/25 to 0500 12/13/25, with higher snow amounts likely towards the east where there was more upslope mountain flow. Given that there was a road closure along the Dalton Highway, 0 mile visibility at Point Thomson for nearly 48 continuous hours, heavy snow reports, and very strong wind gusts, blizzard conditions were safely assumed to have occured.

Multiple posts to a NWS Fairbanks Facebook request for snowfall totals on the afternoon of December 24th revealed 8 to 9 inches of new snowfall over the past 24 hours. Additional snowfall was reported by the Nenana AWOS (PANN) through the afternoon and early evening hours.

Local social media reports indicated 1 inch diameter hail falling near Dot Lake and George Lake. Additional social media reports showed numerous hailstones collected along the Alaska Highway, but likely just under 1 inch in diameter.
